escalations.summary: CrossPeak Solutions moved to Vensure (PEO) and completed benefits enrollment in December 2025, effective January 1, 2026. Vensure's 2026 Benefits Presentation described the coverage as the "2026 plan year," effective "January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026." Beginning in March 2026 — roughly three months after enrollment — Vensure began telling CrossPeak that its ancillary benefits (dental, vision, life, disability, accident, and similar lines) actually run on a July 1–June 30 master plan year and would lapse on June 30, 2026 unless employees actively re-enrolled during a June 17–24 window. This July 1–June 30 ancillary cycle and the active re-enrollment requirement were never disclosed during sales or onboarding. Across roughly nine email threads over eight months, multiple Vensure representatives gave inconsistent answers or non-answers, and a documented commitment to review the contract for ancillary timelines went unanswered. The dispute over what CrossPeak was sold versus what Vensure now asserts remains open; CrossPeak has requested a call with Vensure leadership. On June 17, 2026, CrossPeak confirmed that the signed Benefit Election Contract does state coverage is effective through June 30, 2026 — a detail CrossPeak did not catch and that Vensure never pointed out; the core failure is that this was never surfaced during onboarding.

note.title: Update — Vensure granted the exception; the leadership conversation is still owed
note.html:
Update (June 18, 2026): after escalation, Vensure's benefit leadership approved an exception. Per AVP Brittany Shively, Vensure is "shutting down the ancillary open enrollment"; CrossPeak's ancillary benefits will now align with the January 1 renewal of the medical plan for all future renewals, and CrossPeak "will not be required to renew ancillaries on the 7/1 renewal date." This removes the June 30 lapse risk and the forced mid-year re-enrollment — the outcome CrossPeak asked for. What remains open is the larger conversation: CrossPeak's standing request to meet Vensure's CEO and the account's supporting leadership — reiterated June 26 — has not yet been scheduled.

Confirmed June 17, 2026: the signed Vensure Benefit Election Contract (BEC) does state that the elections and rates are "effective through June 30, 2026." In fairness, that language is in the document CrossPeak signed, and Zane did not catch it at signing.

The issue CrossPeak is raising is not that the date is missing — it is that no one at Vensure ever mentioned, flagged, or walked through the June 30 ancillary cutoff during sales, signing, or onboarding, while Vensure's own 2026 Benefits Presentation simultaneously described the coverage as the "January 1 – December 31, 2026 plan year." Surfacing a buried, consequential end date is exactly what a PEO's onboarding is supposed to do.

Paired with the onboarding failures documented in escalation #04 — where CrossPeak's policy and agreement templates were never requested or loaded — this reflects a significant onboarding miss on Vensure's part, not a one-off oversight.

escalations.summary: While pulling documents for the 2027 medical renewal on September 24, 2026, CrossPeak found that three employees who left earlier in the year — C.W. (termed 3/1/2026), A.K. (4/14/2026) and P.D. (5/4/2026) — were still enrolled and still being billed on CrossPeak's self-funded Trustmark medical plan. Vensure — which enrolled these employees in the plan through its own benefits platform — had terminated all three in payroll on time, and confirmed no premium deductions were still being taken from them. But nothing carried those terminations to the carrier. Under the Benefit Administration Services Addendum signed 11/25/2025, CrossPeak's medical plan was set up on Vensure's 'External Broker of Record' option: Vensure builds the plan, runs enrollment and takes deductions, while updating the carrier on hires, terminations and life events is listed only under Vensure's higher service tiers. The client's stated responsibility is to pay, audit and reconcile the carrier invoice. Trustmark, for its part, directed the group to its broker for changes and to its employer portal to terminate members. No one — Vensure's implementation team, the broker, or the carrier — ever told CrossPeak that it now owned carrier terminations, or set up a process to make sure they happened. Each party assumed another covered it, and CrossPeak paid for it. On September 28, 2026 CrossPeak found the December 2025 record that settles ownership. On 12/19/2025 the broker asked Vensure who needed to be assigned for access to the health plan; Vensure replied 12/23 that "someone from our team" would be assigned. On 12/29/2025 Vensure’s own business consultant wrote that "Nick should have access to be able to pull reports, etc." and asked Vensure’s implementation team to initiate it; the broker replied the same morning, "Access would be great." CrossPeak replied that day, "please let me know if you need anything from my side," and again on 1/5/2026. No one was assigned, the access was never set up, and no one ever asked CrossPeak for anything further. The same gap runs in the other direction: on 9/28/2026 Vensure’s system showed a July hire (H.R.) as enrolled on Trustmark while the broker had never received his enrollment — "There is a disconnect regarding their insurance." Employees were not being onboarded to the carrier, not only offboarded.

note.html:
Vensure proposed it. Brie Dixon (Vensure Business Consultant), 12/29/2025 9:00 AM ET: “All data will be housed in our system. However, Nick should have access to be able to pull reports, etc. @Angel Deaton - does he have access at this time & if not can we please initiate that if the client agrees.”

The broker asked for it. Nick Boeschen (UNIQ), 12/29/2025 9:04 AM ET: “Access would be great…” — and ten days earlier, 12/19/2025 3:49 PM ET: “Who would we need to assign to their health insurance plan to have access…?” Vensure, 12/23/2025 11:36 AM ET: “We will have someone from our team that will be assigned to assist.”

CrossPeak said yes to anything needed. Zane Perry, 12/29/2025 1:25 PM ET: “please let me know if you need anything from my side”; 1/5/2026 6:18 PM ET: “if anybody needs anything from me, please let me know.” Vensure never asked CrossPeak to approve the access, never assigned the promised person, and never set it up.

The result. Vensure holds the only system of record for hires and terminations. The broker confirmed on 9/15/2026: “All the employee data is in the Vensure platform, which I do not have access to.” Without the access Vensure itself proposed, no one outside Vensure could see a hire or a termination — so three terminations never reached the carrier, and at least one new hire’s enrollment never did either.

On the signed addendum. Vensure’s 9/25 position is that the addendum leaves carrier updates to the client and broker. That position depends on the broker having the data. Vensure knew the broker needed report access, said so in writing, promised to assign someone, and did not follow through. This is an implementation failure, it is Vensure’s, and it is the same pattern as #01, #03, #04 and #07: CrossPeak’s account was never properly onboarded.

impact: An estimated ~$25.7K in medical premiums billed for three former employees from April through September 2026, plus roughly $4.8K more if the October bill was paid with them still enrolled (estimate from the January per-member rates; pending the carrier's reconciliation).

Trustmark normally limits retroactive terminations to three months; its 9/30 approval was an exception, not a right CrossPeak could count on.
No process exists today to carry a termination from Vensure's system to the carrier — the gap will repeat on the next departure unless one is created.
